prompt: Produce exactly one concise natural-language caption (a single sentence) that vividly and precisely describes the main subject, visible actions, and setting. Use specific action verbs and name any clear maneuvers; indicate direction of movement (e.g., toward, past, away from) and whether motions are simultaneous. Describe body posture with concrete terms (standing, leaning forward/back, seated upright, reclining, crouching, perched) rather than interpretive labels, and report facial expressions or attention only when visually evident (e.g., smiling, frowning, open mouth, eyes looking toward X). Give precise spatial relationships and scale (next to, behind, in front of, atop, a few feet/meters apart), and note the density or flow of people (isolated, a small group, a line, a crowd). Describe lighting and shadows using observable cues (directional backlight, side light, diffuse/overcast light, strong cast shadows and their direction/length) and include visible surface textures or effects such as wet pavement, puddles, splashes, reflections, or motion blur when present. Keep the caption concrete and image-centered, avoid speculation or subjective judgments unless directly supported by visible evidence.
